rationale: Whole-branch spec fidelity lens, tip 8eaeb05e. Every goal letter (a)-(f) verified as delivered by the INTEGRATED branch, two of them empirically against a binary built from the tip: (a) `mindspec state show` from the spec worktree returns honest `{"mode":"review","activeSpec":...}` with real bd, and with bd unresolvable (`env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`) it exits 1 with an ADR-0035 refusal naming the failed `bd list --type=epic` plus `recovery: mindspec doctor` — the 2026-09-01 `{"mode":""}` exit-0 counterexample is dead; (f) live `mindspec instruct` in review mode renders the frozen-contract rule and the literal `mindspec impl adopt <spec-id> --reason` invocation (both idle.md and review.md carry it; AC-12's rename pin is cobra-anchored in frozen_contract_guidance_test.go). The four plan OQ resolutions are implemented to the letter: OQ-1(a)'s M/R/S/G/T prospective-snapshot protocol is fully present (SnapshotWorktreeTree/ChangedFilesTree in materialize.go, Mindspec-Stage trailer discrimination with fail-closed corrupt/foreign handling, marker CREATE/expected-old CAS publication, landed-detection-before-discriminator ordering at complete.go:737-750, T-stage clear on BOTH terminal paths at :1158, and the committed-range gate leg correctly retained ONLY for reconcile/no-worktree in runCommittedRangeGate); OQ-2's draft carve-out landed as the ADR-0023 amendment (line 204) with the superseded :107/:108 rows struck with supersede annotations, and draft discovery is bd-health-probed so a failed read is never 'not a draft'; OQ-3 option 1 is real (plan.go:514-517 writes ModePlan with its own backward-guard check; next.go advancePhaseOnClaim advances to implement for lifecycle beads only, under the R3.3 lock; SanctionedDerivedSync is the sole unforced backward writer with a lexical single-caller fence); OQ-5's default line is verbatim 'Defaulting to item 1 (bd ready priority order)' on both paths. The proportional claim guard ships WITH the operator notice (next.go:196-197 IgnoredDirtNotice on stderr) and the mandatory ADR-0025 amendment (section at line 61) whose entangleable enumeration was honestly DERIVED non-empty (conditional .gitignore + recording paths) rather than assumed empty — a fidelity-positive refinement of R5.1 with the anti-drift fixtures the spec demands. Filter loudness (exclusion count/reason strings, AC-10b non-empty-set error), pick totality (negative rejected, single-item early return gone), scope honesty (global-fallback removed per R6.7), bd stderr passthrough (20-line cap, termsafe at render), AC-14's total cobra-tree classification with reverse staleness leg, AC-16's four replay legs, and AC-4b's child-read-seam indeterminate form (complete.go:1266-1358, ModePlan message reworded to the two surviving triggers) are all present. The one recovery-hint judgment call I probed — release's SanctionedDerivedSync-failure message naming --force-backward — is correctly disposed: the greppable `recovery:` line is the safe inspection (`bd show`), the force is a separately-labeled operator-choice body line, matching AC-5(iv)'s convention. `mindspec validate docs` at tip: zero errors, only the pre-existing missing-source-globs WARN the BRIEF lists. No silent divergence from the gated design found anywhere I sampled. Confidence is 0.87 rather than higher for one honest reason: my own re-runs of the full-tree `-short` suite and the no-short cmd/mindspec suite were still executing at verdict time under extreme machine contention (~27 concurrent `go test` processes from the 12-slot panel sharing this host); the suites passed every per-bead gate including bead 10's tip run, and nothing in my audit suggests a regression, but my independent confirmation was not yet in hand.

findings.title: Suite re-run confirmation outstanding at verdict time (contention, not failure)
findings.detail: go test ./... -short and go test ./cmd/mindspec -timeout 30m (no -short) were launched from the tip and were still running when this verdict was written, slowed by ~27 concurrent go test processes and heavy shared-Dolt bd contention from the rest of the panel (bd show calls observed taking 30-90s machine-wide). No failure was observed; the tally should confirm one green tip run of each before merge if no other slot supplies it.

findings.title: R5.1 entangleable-path enumeration landed non-empty — richer than the spec's 'empty today' claim, and correctly so
findings.detail: The spec asserted the claim-entangleable user-dirt set is empty today; the landed ComputeEntangleablePaths derived two real conditional classes (.gitignore when the worktree-root entry is absent; the recording events.ndjson/manifest.json when recording is enabled), gated on observed containment, with end-to-end fixtures pinning the enumeration. This is the derived-not-assumed shape R5.1 actually required and re-arms the block for future claim-written paths; recorded here so the divergence from the spec's prose is on the record as adjudicated-faithful, not silent.

findings.title: Environmental: lifecycle verbs serialize behind shared-Dolt bd latency
findings.detail: mindspec instruct took ~2.5 minutes on this host purely waiting on one `bd show mindspec-ta30 --json` child under panel-load contention. Not a branch defect (state show completed in ~1s under the same binary; all bd processes machine-wide were equally slow) — noted so the tally does not mistake similar observations from other slots for a regression introduced by this branch.
